blocks.t: **Objetivo de comunicação (C2):** eu consigo produzir e revisar um parágrafo reformulando-o para ênfase (estrutura de informação, clivadas, inversão e antecipação), seguindo instruções passo a passo.

body: Esta aula treina **ouvir e anotar informações (IELTS Listening, TOEFL Listening)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

blocks.title: How to Revise a Paragraph for Emphasis
paras: **Step 1.** Read the paragraph aloud and **underline the idea that matters most**. **Step 2.** Ask: where does it sit? **If** it is buried mid-sentence, **move it to the end**, where the stress falls. **Step 3.** **Cut** throat-clearing openers (“It is important to note that…”) and **promote** the key noun to the subject.

**Step 4.** Choose **one** device per key point: a pseudo-cleft (“What we need is…”), a cleft (“It is trust that…”), a negative inversion (“Rarely does…”) or a fronted object. **Step 5.** **Check** that no device is **stacked on another**; **three spotlights** equal none. **Finally**, read it aloud again: the **stress** should land **where you meant it**.

items.q: The most important idea should be buried mid-sentence.
The handbook advises using one device per key point.
items.why: Choose one device per key point.

items.q: It recommends using three devices at once for emphasis.

blocks.body: **Estrutura de informação**: o dado conhecido vem antes, o **novo e importante** vem no fim, onde cai o acento. Recursos empilhados (*What it is trust that…*) **anulam** o efeito e geram frases ilegíveis.
Não elimine todos os hedges: *It seems that…* pode ser necessário em ciência. Corte só as aberturas vazias (*It is important to note that*).

body: **Get to the point.** — Ir ao ponto.
**Drive the point home.** — Enfatizar bem.
**Cut the fluff.** — Cortar o enchimento.
**Say it plainly.** — Dizer com clareza.
**Strike a balance.** — Encontrar equilíbrio.
**Hit the nail on the head.** — Acertar na mosca.
**Lay it on thick.** — Exagerar.
**Less is more.** — Menos é mais.
**Make every word count.** — Fazer cada palavra valer.
**Drive home.** — Cravar.
**Where is your main idea?** — Onde está sua ideia principal?
**Buried in the middle of the sentence.** — Soterrada no meio da frase.
**What we need is trust. Better!** — O que precisamos é de confiança. Melhor!

blocks.title: Pronúncia: Ritmo e ênfase para nuances

items.label: Ritmo e ênfase para nuances
items.note: Ritmo e ênfase para nuances: o acento muda o sentido (He said she STOLE it × he said SHE stole it) e as pausas separam ideias técnicas densas.
words: I didn’t SAY he did it.
I didn’t say HE did it.
I didn’t say he DID it.

prompts.q: Revise by moving the idea to the end.
prompts.model: The key to success is trust.
It is trust that drives results.

prompts.q: Read a revised sentence with stress on the key word.

blocks.task: Revise this sentence in two ways: “It is important to note that the budget was the reason for the delay.” Then write a 4-sentence paragraph using one pseudo-cleft, one cleft and one negative inversion.
blocks.model: Version 1: The delay was caused by the budget. Version 2: It was the budget that caused the delay. Paragraph: What delayed the project was money. It was the budget, not the staff, that failed. Rarely have we seen such a gap. Never again will we underestimate costs.

body: Treine esta habilidade com o formato de tarefas curtas das provas (TOEFL/IELTS).
Leia o enunciado primeiro e procure as palavras-chave.
Use exemplos reais da vida dos alunos e peça frases próprias.
Corrija o erro mais frequente da aula em grupo, sem expor o aluno.
Retome o conteúdo na aula seguinte com um exercício curto.
